entries.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control
entries.title: Treasury sanctions ten individuals and one entity over DPRK IT worker fraud, citing cryptocurrency conversions and laundering
entries.facts: On October 28, 2026 the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced that the Office of Foreign Assets Control had designated ten individuals and one entity for their roles in Democratic People's Republic of Korea government-run information-technology worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK's weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs. Four individuals were designated under Executive Order 13687; one entity and six Russia-based DPRK IT workers acting on its behalf were designated under Executive Order 13722. The release states that DPRK IT worker networks use sophisticated cryptocurrency transactions, money laundering techniques and artificial-intelligence tools to generate and transfer millions of dollars, and it attributes to individual designees cryptocurrency conversions of nearly 2 million dollars since January 2025, cryptocurrency exchanges and conversions equivalent to 3.5 million dollars since 2024, cryptocurrency transfers valued at nearly 500,000 dollars since 2024, and the transfer of over 100,000 dollars equivalent in financial assets since at least December 2023. It states the designated entity uses complex cryptocurrency transfers and sophisticated money laundering methods and that the six workers designated alongside it generated over 750,000 dollars for it since 2025. The release states the action builds on OFAC's March 12, 2026 designation of a separate DPRK IT worker network, and it lists no digital currency addresses.
entries.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury press release sb0669, October 28, 2026
entries.relevant_to: digital-asset exchanges, payment processors, banks, sanctions-screening and AML compliance teams

entries.title: CFTC announces a December 15 roundtable on 24/7 trading, listing tokenization among the topics
entries.facts: In Release Number 9318-26 dated October 28, 2026 the Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced that it will host a roundtable on 24/7 trading on December 15 at the Commission's headquarters in Washington. The release states the roundtable will consider whether derivatives markets can viably move to 24/7 trading and lists the topics as overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. It states the dialogue will build upon the Commission's Request for Comment issued earlier in the summer of 2026 on 24/7 trading, and that the agenda, speakers and registration information will be posted at a later date. The release states the roundtable is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov, that in-person attendance may be limited and subject to security screening, and that members of the public may submit speaker nominations by email; it states no nomination deadline. Chairman Selig is quoted as saying, "I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one-size-fits-all approach to 24/7 trading." The release does not mention crypto assets, digital assets, prediction markets or event contracts.
entries.relevant_to: derivatives exchanges and clearing organizations, event-contract and prediction-market platforms, tokenization and digital-asset market infrastructure teams
